To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) A DSP-based digital modulation scheme was designed to eliminate the current spikes at zero-crossing point of AC line.

(a) the transition delay of the low frequency leg causes the current spike at zerocross; (b) the current spike can be eliminated by adding lead time to the high frequency leg; (c) the minimum pulse width of high frequency leg limits the maximum lead time, which can be solved by digital dithering.

(a) the transition delay of the low frequency leg is one of the key causes of the current spike at the zero-crossing point; (b) the minimum pulse width of the high frequency leg is another key cause of the current spike, and (c) the DSP-based digital modulators can effectively solve the above two issues and eliminate the current spike.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a 500 kHz GaNPFC converter using a DSP-based digital control.
a new design method for a GaN-based totem-pole PFC converter with digital control, which can be used in future high power applications.
a new GaN based PFC design and the digital implementation of the modulator to address some inherent challenges of this topology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a well-designed digital modulator is the key enabler for GaN-based totem-pole PFC converter.
the totem-pole PFC converter is a very promising solution for high frequency PFC applications.
the current spike at AC zero-crossing can be avoided by digital modulator design with lead time, digital dithering, and proper timing design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the totem-pole PFC converter is an ideal topology to implement with GaN devices.
the totem-pole converter is a very promising PFC topology for GaN-based high frequency design.
the digital modulator can be applied to the totem-pole PFC circuit with GaN devices to achieve high efficiency and high power density, which is the ultimate goal of the GaN devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of a digital controller for a high frequency GaN-based totem-pole PFC circuit is not as straightforward as a traditional PFC design.
, the current spike issue at zero crossing point of totem-pole PFC converter is not a problem of GaN device itself, but a problem of the topology.
the zero-crossing current spike is not caused by reverse recovery of GaN diode but the transition delay and minimum pulse width limit.
